landmarks.name: Abu Mena
landmarks.description: A UNESCO World Heritage Site — the ruins of the early Christian holy city built over the grave of Saint Menas, a 3rd-century Egyptian martyr. Once one of the greatest pilgrimage centers in the early Christian world, the site includes the remains of a great basilica, a baptistery, baths, and a monastery. Pilgrims came from across the Mediterranean seeking miraculous healing from the sacred waters. The characteristic two-handled flask (ampulla) with Saint Menas praying between two camels became one of the most widely distributed devotional objects in the ancient world.

landmarks.name: Aga Khan Mausoleum
landmarks.description: A stunning pink limestone mausoleum on the west bank of the Nile in Aswan, built for Aga Khan III (Sultan Muhammad Shah), the 48th Imam of the Ismaili Muslims who loved Aswan and spent winters there. A single red rose was placed on the white marble sarcophagus every day by his widow, the Begum, until her death in 2000. landmarks.name: Grand Egyptian Museum (GEM)
landmarks.description: The world's largest archaeological museum dedicated to a single civilization, located 2 km from the Giza Pyramids. At a cost of $1.2 billion, the GEM houses over 100,000 artifacts across 12 permanent galleries arranged chronologically from prehistory to the Greco-Roman period. Its crown jewel is the complete 5,398-piece Tutankhamun collection displayed together for the first time. The museum spans 500,000 square meters with a dramatic glass-roofed atrium housing an 11-meter, 83-ton Ramesses II colossus, a monumental grand staircase with 60+ artifacts, the reconstructed Khufu Solar Boats, a children's museum with AR experiences, and 19 conservation laboratories. Officially inaugurated on November 1, 2025 — the anniversary of Tutankhamun's tomb discovery — it received 18,000 visitors on its first public day.

landmarks.name: Nile Cruise (Luxor to Aswan)
landmarks.description: The quintessential Egyptian experience — a multi-day cruise along the Nile between Luxor and Aswan (or vice versa), tracing the route of pharaohs and Victorian-era explorers. Most cruises span 3-7 nights, stopping at Edfu Temple, Kom Ombo Temple, and the Esna Lock along the way. Passengers wake to ever-changing riverscapes of palm-fringed banks, feluccas gliding past, and ancient temples emerging from the horizon. Options range from luxurious 5-star floating hotels to traditional dahabiyas (wooden sailing boats). The journey offers a unique perspective on rural Egyptian life along the fertile Nile Valley.

landmarks.name: Wadi Degla Protectorate
landmarks.description: A stunning desert canyon and nature reserve just 10 minutes from Maadi in Cairo's eastern suburbs. The 60 km² protectorate preserves a dramatic wadi (dry riverbed) with towering limestone cliffs up to 50 meters high, home to Dorcas gazelles, Nubian ibex, foxes, and over 18 species of reptiles. Popular with hikers, cyclists, and trail runners, the main trail follows the wadi floor for 4 km through spectacular geological formations revealing 60 million years of marine fossils.
